---
title: "Architecture: a controlled baseline and structural ladders"
---

> **Reading note.** This is an explanatory reconstruction of Jiaxuan Zou’s literature synthesis. Published experiments belong to the cited teams. Numbered protocols and illustrative matrices are our planning synthesis unless explicitly attributed.

The blog's §4 separates fixed settings, prescribed scaling rules, and independent experimental variables. An architecture ladder is interpretable only when it states which of these roles each setting plays.

## Concrete empirical starting point

Read [the width/depth and μP evidence guide](../architecture/architecture-evidence.qmd) for exact published configurations. AI2’s ladder uses widths 768/1,024/1,536/2,048 with depths 12/16/16/16; its target depths are 32/40. This is a task-prediction experiment, not an isolated depth-optimization sweep. The guide compares that practice with fixed-depth μP transfer and explicit shape studies. [Bhagia et al., v2, §2.1/Table 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.04403v2#S2.T1).

## Step-by-step protocol

1. Start from a target-compatible decoder baseline. Freeze tokenizer, normalization, activation, positional encoding, embedding tying, attention family, context length, precision, and initialization.
2. Declare a width/depth progression. For each configuration, record hidden width, layer count, head dimension, attention groups, MLP dimension, trunk parameters, and output-head cost.
3. Sweep aspect ratio at matched parameter or compute budgets as a separate ablation. Retune enough to avoid mistaking optimization difficulty for inferior architecture.
4. For MoE, separate active-size scaling, expert-count/sparsity scaling, and expert-granularity sweeps. Keep routing, balancing, shared experts, and drop behavior explicit.
5. Measure throughput and memory on the intended hardware. Compare equivalent quality at a training and serving cost the project can afford.
6. Validate the winning structure at a larger scale and at the intended token horizon and precision.

For a rough dense baseline, $N_{\mathrm{body}}\approx12d^2n$. Holding $N_{\mathrm{body}}$ fixed means increasing width $d$ forces depth $n$ downward under this approximation. This changes sequential computation and attention's relative cost, so equal parameter counts do not imply equal wall-clock time.

## Minimal run matrix

| Family | Size tiers | Structural variable | Controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dense baseline | Three fitting tiers | Prescribed width/depth rule | Fixed primitives and token horizon |
| Aspect-ratio ablation | Two or more tiers | Width/depth at matched budget | Comparable tuning |
| MoE candidate | Separate tiers | One of sparsity or granularity | Fixed active-size convention |
| Holdout | Larger unseen tier | Selected complete architecture | Frozen recipe |

This matrix is an illustrative planning template, not a budget recommendation or a published optimum.

**Acceptance checklist:** comparable compute accounting; no boundary winner left unexplored; numerical stability; downstream task floors; memory and throughput constraints; fresh holdout after recipe selection.

**Sources:** [blog §4 and §5.6](../reading/scientific-scaling-ladder.md#4-baseline-recipe-and-scaling-rules); [Gemstones, 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.06857); [Krajewski et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07871); [OLMoE, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02060).
